causal-factors.rationale: H.R. 33 passed the House by a 423-1 vote, signaling strong bipartisan support and potential momentum for Senate action (sources: turn0search2, turn5search7).

causal-factors.rationale: Historically, only a small fraction of introduced federal bills become law (commonly around 2-6%, with some periods below 1%), making enactment unlikely absent decisive Senate action (sources: turn2search2, turn2search0).

causal-factors.rationale: Historical precedent shows enacted-law rates for introduced bills are low, and recent output has been modest, suggesting limited odds of rapid enactment absent Senate action; 2025 saw fewer than 40 bills signed into law and the 119th Congress had a limited number of public laws by early 2026. (sources: Washington Post discussion of overall enactment rates; National Archives snapshot of 119th Congress public laws) ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record/volume-171/issue-11/extensions-of-remarks-section/article/E49-3?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The baseline ensemble estimate is 2%, but recent House momentum and ongoing tax-policy negotiations create a plausible upside. However, without Senate action and presidential approval, enactment by May 1, 2026 remains unlikely, justifying a small but nonzero probability around 5%.
